name: AI evals and agents
summary: Whether a PM has actually built AI quality systems, from the Evals for PMs course and Reforge notes: defining good, trace reading, triage, code checks vs judges, calibration, datasets, iteration, monitoring, agent decomposition, autonomy.

nodes.label: Defining good
nodes.about: Turning quality into a written bar: rubric, thresholds, golden examples, an 'I don't know' policy.

tests.question: Does the speaker describe a written quality bar with specific criteria or thresholds (not engagement or thumbs-up)?
tests.probe: Ask what a failing output looked like, in their last product.

tests.question: Does the speaker treat 'I don't know' or abstaining as a designed behaviour with an expected rate?
tests.probe: Ask how often the system should say it doesn't know, and what rate would worry them.

nodes.label: Reading traces
nodes.about: Manual error analysis of real traces before automating: free-form notes, clustering into failure codes, saturation.

tests.question: Does the speaker describe personally reading real traces or outputs and categorising failures before building automated evals?
tests.probe: Ask how many traces they read before writing their first eval, and what they found.

tests.question: Does the speaker treat a trace as more than the chat transcript (tool calls, retrieval, intermediate steps)?
tests.probe: Ask what was in a trace besides the user's message and the answer.

nodes.label: What becomes an eval
nodes.about: Separating spec gaps (fix the prompt), architecture gaps (engineering) and generalisation gaps (worth an eval).

tests.question: Does the speaker distinguish failures that are fixed directly (prompt or engineering bugs) from those that need an ongoing eval?
tests.probe: Ask about a failure they fixed without writing an eval for it.

nodes.label: Code checks vs judges
nodes.about: Deterministic checks first, LLM judges for the subjective remainder.

tests.question: Does the speaker use deterministic code checks (format, presence, tool-call sequence, thresholds) before or alongside LLM judges?
tests.probe: Ask which of their checks didn't need a model at all.

tests.question: Does the speaker prefer binary pass/fail judges with one criterion each over 1-to-10 quality scores?
tests.probe: Ask what the judge's prompt actually said pass looks like.

nodes.label: Judge calibration
nodes.about: Measuring judge agreement with expert labels: TPR/TNR, confusion matrix, dev/test split, recalibration.

tests.question: Does the speaker describe measuring the judge against human labels, with separate true-positive and true-negative rates or a confusion matrix, not one agreement percentage?
tests.probe: Ask how often the judge passed something a human would fail.

nodes.label: Datasets
nodes.about: Building eval sets: hard cases over common ones, size, synthetic vs production data, versioning, contamination.

tests.question: Does the speaker build datasets around hard or failure cases rather than mirroring traffic frequency?
tests.probe: Ask where the hardest cases in their set came from.

tests.question: Does the speaker give concrete dataset sizes or splits and how they changed over time?
tests.probe: Ask how big the set was at launch and six months later.

nodes.label: Iteration
nodes.about: Changing one thing at a time, reporting deltas per eval, knowing the noise floor.

tests.question: Does the speaker describe changing one variable at a time and reading per-eval deltas and failing traces, rather than 'overall quality improved'?
tests.probe: Ask about a change that looked like a win and turned out to be noise.

nodes.label: Production monitoring
nodes.about: Online evals, sampling, drift, user signals, alert ownership.

tests.question: Does the speaker describe monitoring quality in production (sampled judges, drift, user edits or corrections) beyond thumbs-up rates?
tests.probe: Ask how they found out about the last quality regression in production.

nodes.label: Agent decomposition
nodes.about: Evaluating agents step by step: routing, tool selection and parameters, handoffs, failure funnels, recovery.

tests.question: Does the speaker break the agent into steps (routing, tool choice, parameters, response handling) and evaluate each, rather than only end-to-end?
tests.probe: Ask which step of the agent failed most, and how they knew.

tests.question: Does the speaker show awareness that step accuracies multiply (e.g. seven steps at 95% is about 70% end to end) or name the earliest bottleneck?
tests.probe: Ask what end-to-end success rate they'd expect from seven steps at 95% each.

nodes.label: Autonomy and review
nodes.about: Where the agent acts alone vs proposes; human review limits; reversibility; override rate and trust.

tests.question: Does the speaker set autonomy by reversibility and cost of error, with a measure such as override rate, rather than 'add a human in the loop'?
tests.weak: "Human in the loop" as the whole answer
tests.probe: Ask which actions the agent could take without review, and what would earn it more.
